headline: Advance Summer and Autumn Reservations Required
reservation: White Mountain National Forest does not require a general entry permit, but specific backcountry sites and Appalachian Mountain Club huts require advance booking. State park areas like Franconia Notch often utilize a separate parking reservation system during peak foliage and summer weekends; verify current official procedures before arrival.

days.title: High Peaks and Notch Exploration

stops.name: Franconia Notch State Park
stops.detail: Walk the Flume Gorge boardwalk to see 90-foot granite walls and cascading water.

stops.name: Mount Lafayette via Franconia Ridge
stops.detail: For experienced hikers, this ridge offers a granite spine with 360-degree views of the Presidential Range.

days.driving: Allow 1-2 hours; conditions vary with weekend foliage traffic.
days.note: Early arrivals are necessary as trailheads at the Notch often reach capacity by mid-morning.

days.title: The Iconic Mountain Byway

stops.name: Kancamagus Highway
stops.detail: Drive this 34-mile scenic route for river overlooks and historic covered bridges.

stops.name: Sabbaday Falls
stops.detail: Take a short walk to a multi-tiered waterfall and a natural pothole carved by glacial melt.

days.driving: Allow 3-4 hours; no fuel or services are available on the highway stretch.
days.note: Autumn weekends result in significantly slower travel times due to leaf-peeping crowds.

days.title: Northeastern Summits

stops.name: Mount Washington Auto Road
stops.detail: Drive to the 6,288-foot summit to experience extreme alpine weather and the summit museum.

stops.name: Diana's Baths
stops.detail: Visit these gentle cascades and shallow pools for a relaxing final afternoon in the woods.

days.driving: Allow 2-3 hours; Auto Road descent requires low gears and brake cooling stops.
days.note: Check the summit weather forecast daily; conditions frequently diverge from valley temperatures.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: Parking lots at Franconia Notch and the Kancamagus Highway fill early during summer. Have a secondary trail choice ready in case your primary destination is inaccessible.

intel.title: Communication Gaps
intel.text: Cellular reception is highly unreliable throughout the forest interior and deep notches. Download offline maps at your gateway town before entering the national forest boundary.

intel.title: Mountain Gateway Supply
intel.text: Fill your tank in Lincoln or North Conway before starting the Kancamagus Highway. There are no refueling stations for the entire 34-mile duration of Route 112.

intel.title: Seasonal Mud Window
intel.text: High-elevation trails remain saturated through late May or early June. Stick to lower-elevation paths during this 'mud season' to prevent significant trail erosion.

intel.title: Winter Road Closures
intel.text: Several forest service roads close to vehicles from December through May. Check official Forest Service alerts for current gate statuses before winter outings.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at Portland International Jetport (PWM) and drive approximately 2.5 hours to North Conway to stock up on groceries and mountain gear.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for main roads; check rental agreements for restrictions on the Mount Washington Auto Road.
plan.goldenHour: Mount Willard Overlook offers a dramatic view of Crawford Notch at sunset, subject to seasonal cloud cover.
